findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed an employee fail to use a barrier to turn off the faucet after handwashing. Education was conducted and proper handwashing was observed. Ensure staff are using a paper towel to turn off the hand sink. The faucet is handled with dirty hands and is therefore a contamination point for clean hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed no sanitizer spray or buckets available during food preparation. The PIC was informed that a sanitizer solution must be accessible at all times during food preparation or service. A sanitizer spray bottle was prepared during the inspection, measuring 200ppm quaternary ammonia. Ensure these spray bottles are prepared prior to starting food service.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the dish machine in the kitchen measure 0ppm chlorine. The PIC was informed and discovered that the sanitizer solution hooked up to the machine has evaporated and weakened in concentration. The bucket of sanitizer was replaced, but the issue did not improve after multiple runs. Ecolab was contacted during the visit to request service. In the meantime, staff are required to place all dish-ware in a sanitizer solution following washing and rinsing in the dish machine. Ensure all dishes are fully submerged in the sink to guarantee proper sanitization. 
A follow-up will be conducted on October 12, 2026 to ensure the dish machine is repaired. Please contact the inspector if the machine is repaired sooner than the follow-up date.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the heat sanitizing dish machine at the bar to be reaching temperatures between 130-150F. Discussed using a temporary sanitizer set up using quaternary ammonia until the machine is serviced (verify with test strips), OR taking to kitchen dish machine or triple sink. Ensure food contact surfaces are sanitized using a chemical solution that reaches the concentration for sanitation of food contact surfaces as recommended by the manufacturer's label until the machine is serviced. Inspector will return on or by April 20 to verify the dish machine is reaching a minimum sanitizing temperature of 160F.
findings.citation_text: 4-703.11(B) Hot Water and Chemical. After being cleaned, equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in: (B) Hot water mechanical operations by being cycled through EQUIPMENT that is set up as specified under §§ 4-501.15, 4-501.112, and 4-501.113 and achieving a UTENSIL surface temperature of 71°C (160°F) as measured by an irreversible registering temperature indicator.[P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed sanitizer bottles to register a concentration of 100 ppm quaternary ammonia. CORRECTED- the sanitizer bottles were remade to proper concentration- 200 ppm (200-400 ppm is required for quaternary ammonia). Discussed letting the line run for a few seconds before filling the bottles in the future. Ensure sanitizer solutions are tested to verify they are reaching chemical sanitizing concentration as recommended by the manufacturer's label.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.[P]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a mushroom sauce in the walk in cooler to be held past it’s 7 day date mark (4/2). CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) stated the sauce will be discarded. Ensure all temperature control for food safety (TCS) foods are date marked to be used or discarded within seven days- the day of preparation/ opening/ thawing counts as day ONE.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.[Pf]

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.comment: Inspector observed an unlabeled bottle containing a clear liquid in the kitchen. CORRECTED- bottle was confirmed to be sanitizer and labeled accordingly. Ensure all chemicals removed from bulk containers are labeled to prevent contamination of food and nonfood contact surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 7-102.11 Common Name. Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material. [Pf]

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the facility does not have a way to verify sanitizing temperatures of the bar dish machine. Discussed the need for a heat plate or irreversible measuring test strips for heat sanitation of food contact surfaces. Inspector will check for compliance on or by April 27, 2026. Ensure the facility obtains a dish plate or heat strips to verify minimum heat sanitizing temperatures of 160F.
findings.citation_text: 4-302.13(B) Temperature Measuring Devices, Manual and Mechanical Warewashing. (B) In hot water mechanical WAREWASHING operations, an irreversible registering temperature indicator shall be provided and readily accessible for measuring the UTENSIL surface temperature. [Pf]

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the steam table in the back corner of the kitchen to be holding food at 125F. Discussed with. PIC, and figured out that the hot-holding unit was turned down too low. Food was reheated for holding at 10AM according to kitchen staff, and service is over at 2pm. In this instance, discard the food after service. Food is allowed to be held at ambient temp for up to 4 hours before being discarded. Corrected: PIC turned the hot holding on a warmer setting, inspector probed at 135F before leaving. Ensure hot holding units are kept at 135F or above and checked regularly.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.
